Should we consider the Six Kings Slam an exhibition event, or an alternative pro circuit event? What the title says. Personally, considering the HUGE money incentive to win it, I think it should be seen as a professional invitational event, in the vein of the pre-Open Era Pro Tour of the Gonzales/Rosewall/Laver era. Also, there's an actual betting market for it, which generally isn't the case for "true" exhibition events. What I believe is happening, is that the tournament organization are trying to play it down as "technically" an exho, so that the ATP doesn't slam the door on them by changing the rules to prevent top players from taking part in what really is a budding alternative circuit in all but name. Opinions?

What players other than Federer achieved these results past their peak? According to many Federer's peak ended in 2007. But after 2007 Federer achieved: - the majority of his Slam finals (17 out of 31) - the majority of his Slam semifinals (30 out of 46) - the majority of his big tournaments finals (52 out of 92) - the majority of his big tournament semifinals (84 out of 130) What other players have reached the majority of Slam F/SFs and Big Tournament F/SFs after their peak ended?

Hence, to make the match-up at least fairer, I decided to give 2026 Alcaraz (arguably his peak AO form, especially in the finals) the serve of John Isner, while preserving everything else in his game. No male tennis players get a D1 “full ride”. I am surprised to come here and see people that are in the tennis world , and still inquire about “full rides”, There are usually 10 or more players on a D1 tennis team. They offer 4.5 scholarships. (I guess might offer. Is not mandatory) (Rules are changing, and it seems some might offer 10, but there is no rule that they must so nobody knows) we just know women’s sports must offer more to make up for football scholarships going to boys due to title IX. So let’s say a tennis team has on average 2-3 openings a year. And let’s say you are a 12.5 utr. One of the top 10, 20, or 50 players in all Of the USA. If that school gives you a “full ride” that leaves 3.5 for the rest of the team. You are just an incoming freshman. Even if you are top of your high school class, it does not mean you are top of the university. You most likely will be near the bottom of the line up. Even if you are top of the line up, not many coaches want to leverage it like that. Many of the other players would not return if their partial was given to an incoming freshman. Now if someone can help me here…. Even if your top player gets a partial scholarship, if they are going out of state , aren’t they paying increased tuition? Example. UGA cost in state. $29,000 UGA cost out of state $52,000 So if an out of state player gets a partial scholarship, aren’t they paying based on the $52,000?

After this USO, it needs to be said Federer's run from the first round of 2004 to the final of 2009 looks more and more impressive the more time passes on. Since his remarkable run, we know of at least four ATG players that have won the USO, Nadal, Djokovic, Sinner and Alcaraz, plus several players who had the potential to play like an ATG player = Murray, Wawrinka, Del Potro, Cilic, Medvedev, Thiem, and now Zverev. That is a list of a who's who of the top tier talent from the several generations that followed Federer's....and yet none of them could go back to back Federer went back to back four times, and all four of them were in succession. I don't care about what people think the competition was, to do what he did does indeed deserve praise because even defending the title once has been impossible for a true hall of fame list of HC talents, and this guy ruled NYC with an iron fist. Say what you want about him. Think what you want about him. But you cannot deny his greatness.
